titolo: Zelensky's Warship Strike in Libya Has Allies Panicking
angolo: Day 3: Kyiv's legal case under Article 51 vs. the human cost in Libya and the political squeeze on Italy's Meloni
descrizione: Zelensky's Warship Strike in Libya Has Allies Panicking. Ukraine says sinking the Russian corvette Merkury in Benghazi was lawful self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Two Libyan soldiers have since died, both Libyan governments condemned the strike, and Italy's foreign minister says the war must not spread to the Mediterranean. Here is what is confirmed, what is only claimed, and what Moscow and Rome say comes next.

scene.testo: Night. A Russian warship capsizes in a harbor in Africa, Ukraine says it sank it.
Seven sea drones, Ukraine says. Built in Ukraine. Used thousands of kilometers from the front line.
Now two Libyan military personnel are dead, the Libyan National Army says, and the region is asking who is next.
Can Ukraine legally strike a Russian warship inside a third country's port?
That is the question Kyiv answered on Tuesday. Tripoli is not convinced.
Stay with me. Two numbers from Libya matter here.
Let's rewind to Sunday, November 22.
Ukraine's security service says its drones hit the corvette Merkury in Benghazi harbor.
A second Russian ship, the cargo vessel Angara, was also hit, Ukraine says.
Zelensky called it an exemplary Ukrainian operation.
Satellite imagery reported by CNBC shows the warship mostly underwater, capsized.
Libyan officials told the Associated Press the ship was only heavily damaged, according to Al Jazeera.
Zelensky said a Ka-27 helicopter aboard was destroyed too.
Who is the man who ordered this?
Volodymyr Zelensky, president of Ukraine, leading a country at war with Russia.
Kyiv says it will keep operating. Moscow says its strikes on Ukraine will continue.
First, the legal fight. Ukraine's foreign minister addressed it on Tuesday.
Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called it a legitimate act of self-defence.
He pointed to Article 51 of the United Nations Charter.
Kyiv's foreign ministry spokesman Heorhii Tykhyi went further.
Sybiha said Russian naval vessels and cargo ships carrying military equipment were valid targets.
Sybiha also said Ukraine respects Libya's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
Libya's Tripoli-based government condemned the strike, and the eastern government has also protested to the UN.
Tripoli's foreign ministry said it condemns any foreign military operation on Libyan territory or in its waters.
It said the war between Russia and Ukraine gives neither side the right to conduct military operations on Libyan territory or in its waters.
Tripoli also demanded official clarifications from Kyiv.
Musa al-Koni, vice chair of Libya's Presidential Council, said Ukraine's claim of the attack could be considered a declaration of war, TASS reports.
The United Nations mission in Libya called for an independent investigation.
It also warned against dragging Libya into foreign conflicts.
Then came Tuesday, and the human cost.
Saddam Haftar, son of eastern commander Khalifa Haftar, announced on social media that two naval personnel had died.
The Libyan National Army named the two dead as Al-Taher Abdullah al-Sadiq and Lt. Ali Mohammed al-Said.
The Libyan National Army says its response will come at the appropriate time and place.
The Kremlin stayed silent for more than 24 hours, Dagens reported, before Peskov spoke on Monday.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Monday that Moscow had taken note of Zelensky's statement.
He said the defence ministry would release details if it deemed it appropriate.
He called the Ukrainian operation off Libya and the Baltic attacks a very dangerous trend.
And he said Russia's strikes on Ukraine have very painful consequences for the Kyiv regime.
He pointed back to a statement Putin made in Shenzhen.
Peskov said Russia's military continues large-scale daily strikes on military infrastructure in Ukraine.
But one of the loudest reactions came from Rome.
Italy's foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, spoke with Sybiha on Tuesday, according to Italy's foreign ministry.
The ministry says he stressed respect for Libya's sovereignty and keeping the conflict out of the Mediterranean.
Tajani told reporters Italy had not been informed about the attack, according to Euronews.
Here is how Tajani put the worry.

citazione.testo: If this is a continuation of the war between Russia and Ukraine just a few hundred kilometers from Italy, this is worrying, especially because we work for the stability of Libya.

scene.testo: Why does Libya matter so much to Italy?
It is a former Italian colony, Politico notes.
Politico says the strikes could become a headache for Giorgia Meloni.
Politico says she stands out in Europe for her strong backing of Ukraine.
Politico says that puts her at odds with part of her own coalition.
League leader and Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini questioned whether aid to Ukraine should end up sinking ships around the world.
He also warned the war reaching North Africa risks being a bomb that explodes in Italy's house, Giornale di Sicilia reports.
Meloni has not commented publicly, according to Euronews.
La Repubblica reports she privately called the attacks unacceptable. That is unconfirmed.
Greece's defence minister, Nikos Dendias, demanded an explanation from Kyiv, according to Athens News.
So how did Zelensky answer his worried allies?
Is this part of something bigger?
An EU official told Euronews Ukraine wanted to signal that Russian vessels in the Mediterranean are within reach.
Al Jazeera notes Ukraine is also stepping up attacks on Russian-linked ships, including in the Baltic.
Three questions now decide what comes next.
One: will Libya's armies answer, as the LNA promises?
Two: will the UN investigation requested by Libya's eastern government actually happen?
Three: will Rome's concerns change Kyiv's calculations? Nothing official says so yet.
Ukraine's position: Russian warships and arms carriers are legitimate targets.
Russia's position: a dangerous trend with painful consequences.
Libya's position: neither side has the right to fight on its territory or in its waters.
Italy's position: keep this war out of the Mediterranean, and respect Libya's sovereignty.
